prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Hearts of Iron IV inline stockpile-cost texticon, one static frame, exact final canvas 30x12 pixels; displayed directly beside a numeric prepared-biological-payload cost.
Input images: Image 1 is a canonical Vanilla HOI4 modifier-family style reference only. Transfer only the restrained aged-material rendering, compact painted shading, and dark edge treatment. Do not copy its supply-can silhouette, geometry, colors, arrangement, or markings.
Primary request: Create one original military inventory glyph for prepared biological payload stock. It must read as a compact biological delivery bomb or sealed bio-payload vial, not as a chemical pressure canister or nuclear missile.
Scene/backdrop: No scene or floor. The unused canvas must be genuinely transparent.
Subject: One squat, sealed capsule-shaped biological bomb with a rounded body, short tapered nose, and two small tail fins or tabs. Add a distinct, simple biohazard glyph stenciled directly onto a small light casing band; keep the mark large and bold enough to survive at 30x12.
Style/medium: Compact painted 2D inventory art with modest 1930s–1940s military materials, muted slate, olive-drab, and aged brass, a small dark biohazard marking, restrained highlights, and crisp dark edge definition.
Composition/framing: Center one broad, horizontal but visibly squat bomb/vial silhouette. Design its visible silhouette for a 30x12 inline glyph: about 2.2:1 width-to-height, simple readable outer shape, complete inset edges, and enough transparent margin to avoid clipping. On the source canvas, use a centered horizontal strip with the glyph spanning most of the width and roughly two fifths of the height.
Lighting/mood: Even understated icon lighting; small metallic highlights only.
Constraints: Genuine transparent background from the first render; no text, letters, numbers, watermark, fumes, extra objects, scene, tile, frame, border, badge, medallion, or separate emblem. The biohazard cue is a simple marking directly on the bomb casing, not a separate badge. Keep one subject only and do not reproduce Image 1. Optimize the silhouette and hazard cue for readability after smooth downsampling to 30x12.
Avoid: A long rocket or nuclear-missile profile, chemical jerrycan shape, oversized badge, bright neon colors, chrome shine, modern equipment, cinematic lighting, fake checkerboard, opaque matte, colored halo, unintended transparent holes.
